newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may begin K&H bank sell-off in Dec - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may begin K&H bank sell-off in Dec - paper.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV may sell a stake of 30 to 35 percent in its third largest commercial bank, Kereskedelmi Bank Rt (K&H) this year, the daily Vilaggazdasag said on Thursday.
APV plans to take up the discussion of a planned capital increase on the agenda of the meeting of K&H shareholders on December 20, the paper said.
The Finance Ministry said earlier this week that it planned to boost K&H's equity by some $60 million this year or in 1997.
Part of that amount would be a 6 billion forint capital increase to be subscribed by a closed circle of financial investors, Vilaggazdasag said, citing unnamed sources.
The price of the shares, which would represent a 30 to 35 percent stake in the bank, is likely to be around 110 percent of the face value, the paper added.
Hungary sold a controlling stake in MHB, its fifth largest bank, to Dutch ABN AMRO earlier this month.
K&H is the last large Hungarian bank awaiting privatisation.
